## 固定收益市場主線

10月9日，美國公債回吐部分由標售帶動的漲幅。能源價格居高不下，家庭通膨預期又上升，聯準會進一步升息的可能性持續牽動市場。賣壓集中在短、中天期：2年期殖利率上升2.92個基點至4.7869%，10年期上升1.1個基點至5.2378%；30年期則小降0.45個基點至5.5956%。殖利率曲線因而趨平，長債並未再度全面遭到拋售。

密西根大學初步調查是當天最明確的經濟新訊。消費者信心降幅超過預期，對當前景氣的評估降至歷史低點，兩項通膨預期也同步上升。家庭面臨的壓力清晰可見，卻沒有提供明確的通膨降溫訊號。儘管盤中一度因外交與供給消息獲得喘息，布蘭特原油仍收在每桶$104.72，上漲0.42%。

其他市場較能承受當天的波動。美國高收益債利差小幅收窄，強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債利差明顯收窄，股市也回升。不過，最新部位資料顯示投資人減少利率敏感度較高的公債期貨曝險；歐洲主權債波動讓ECB例行流動性工具受到關注，企業融資情況則持續分化。Firmus正式放棄澳洲上市，轉向尋求私募資金；DayOne仍在初步洽談發債；Virgin Media O2一項資產交易受阻的風險使降槓桿更為複雜，債券價格進一步下跌。高水準的絕對殖利率仍吸引買盤，但能否取得資金，愈來愈取決於借款人的條件、現金創造能力與契約保障。

## 家庭通膨預期升溫，美國公債曲線趨平

週五美國公債的跌幅小於前一交易日的漲幅，各基準殖利率全週仍然下降。5年期殖利率上升2.68個基點至5.0157%，與2年期同為曲線中表現較弱的部分。2年與10年期利差縮小1.82個基點至45.09個基點，2年與30年期利差縮小3.37個基點至80.87個基點。本週標售順利，支撐最長天期公債；對政策前景較敏感的債券價格則下跌。

全週2年、5年、10年與30年期殖利率分別下降4.01、3.83、3.52與2.54個基點，相較過去一個月大幅重新定價，只是稍獲喘息。10年期仍比一個月前高44.78個基點，30年期高34.96個基點；2年期也上升39.19個基點，顯示壓力不只來自長端供給與財政疑慮。

週五10年期名目殖利率上升，來自實質殖利率的變化。10年期TIPS殖利率上升2.23個基點至2.8851%，損益兩平通膨率則下降1.13個基點至2.3527%。過去一個月實質殖利率上升47.01個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降2.23個基點。能源仍是政策辯論的核心，但當天市場呈現的組合，是扣除通膨後的融資成本提高、較長期通膨補償下降。

密西根大學10月初步消費者信心指數由48.1降至46.3，低於市場預期的47.6。汽油價格、借貸成本與招聘放緩壓迫家庭，現況指數從50.9降至44.7，創歷史新低；對未來景氣的預期指數則由46.3改善至47.3。因此，信心惡化主要集中在當前情況的評估，並非調查各項目全面轉差。

通膨預期朝相反方向變化：較短期的預期由4.6%升至4.7%，5年期預期由3.4%升至3.5%。Bloomberg報導也指出，消費者對耐久財購買條件的評估降至歷史低點。家庭一方面感到負擔能力下降，另一方面預期物價壓力加重，使聯準會更難在進一步抑制通膨與等待近期市場利率上升壓低需求之間取捨。

聯準會週五公布的消費者財務調查，則從較長期間呈現家庭承受能力的另一面。截至2025年的三年間，家庭淨資產中位數上升2%至$21萬5,900，平均淨資產上升7%至$124萬1,500。低收入家庭薪資小幅成長，高收入者所得下降，收入不均因而收斂；但收入最高的一成家庭，其平均財富仍超過收入最低兩成家庭的50倍。

2022年至2025年間，S&P 500上漲近80%，持股家庭占比卻由58%降至56%，參與率減少幾乎全數來自收入分布下半部家庭。有負債的家庭比例維持77%，但債務償付占所得超過40%的家庭達8.6%，為2010年以來最高。這份歷史調查有助解釋股市強勁與家庭信心低迷為何能同時存在：資產增值分配不均，融資支出卻需要動用當期所得。

週五風險資產回升，仍顯示市場對企業獲利有信心。S&P 500上漲0.59%至7,811.54，Nasdaq 100上漲0.51%，半導體股則再跌0.41%；VIX降至14.84。Bloomberg的市場報導指出，S&P 500成分股僅約三分之一站上50日均線，Russell 2000成分股更只有27%。大型指數的韌性，與規模較小、對利率較敏感企業的弱勢並存。

美元小幅走強，美元指數上升0.07%至102.21。另一項指標Bloomberg美元即期指數連續第四週上漲，期間累計約3%，為2025年初以來最長連漲。CFTC截至10月6日的資料顯示，美元多頭押注超過$350億。CIBC的Sarah Ying認為，避險需求、歐洲財政疑慮與荷姆茲海峽供給受威脅帶動美元需求；PGIM的Robert Tipp則強調，美國相較其他經濟體更能承受較高利率。

新的研究與部位資料，為近期公債走勢提供更廣的背景。紐約聯準銀行期限溢價模型顯示，自9月中以來，期限溢價上升約40個基點至約0.98%，達2014年以來最高；增幅甚至超過同一期間10年期殖利率近30個基點的漲幅。另一項納入經濟學家政策預測的估計升至1.08%，為2010年以來最高。這些模型估計反映持有利率風險所要求的補償；Barclays研究人員指出，總體不確定性、股債相關性改變、債務供給與財政疑慮，都可能有所貢獻。

週五公布的CFTC資料，則具體呈現曝險縮減。截至10月6日的兩週內，資產管理機構削減超長天期美國公債期貨多頭部位，每基點風險金額約減少$2,700萬，相當於約$380億的當期10年期現券。Bloomberg將這波賣盤與最便宜可交割券的變動連結：可交割券改變使投資組合存續期間拉長。超長天期期貨未平倉量連續七個交易日下降，每基點風險金額累計減少近$2,000萬。這些部位與先前交易的變化，說明技術性賣壓如何加強長債的基本面重新定價。

Citi在週五較晚發布的報告中，提出財政部可能調整供給的預測。美國利率策略師Jason Williams預期，11月4日再融資公告將把20年與30年期標售規模各削減$30億，改以增加國庫券填補資金需求；他也提出取消20年期標售的可能性。其論點在於退休基金需求可能轉向長天期、高品質科技公司債，並未把整體利率水準歸因於這些企業發債。這項預測為公債期限配置的討論提出具體調整規模；10月16日的交易商問卷可能透露財政部對此議題的關注程度。

## 歐洲債價回穩，融資壓力仍在

週五盤中油價回落、法國政治消息暫趨平靜，歐洲公債因而穩定。Bloomberg交易報導顯示，法國10年期公債相對德國的利差縮小3個基點至137個基點，另一項盤中觀察曾低至135個基點。法國殖利率下降3個基點至4.86%，讓法債朝六週來首次週線上漲邁進，義大利公債則接近九週來首次週線上漲。

不過，相對定價仍凸顯法國與鄰國的差異。即使大盤回穩，法國與義大利10年期殖利率差距週五仍達30個基點，創歐元成立以來紀錄。Aegon的Irina Kurochkina表示，投資人趁近期利差擴大買進義大利與西班牙債券，卻大致避開法國。Jefferies的Mohit Kumar認為，風險在於買家可能停止承接，而非主權債重整危機；他預期避險基金會在反彈時增加空頭部位。他並判斷，法德利差可能要接近200個基點，ECB才會採取口頭表態以外的干預。

流動性問題也超出主權信用範圍。歐元區超額準備金已從四年前逾€4.5兆降向€2兆，附買回利率升至2025年3月以來最高。銀行透過ECB一週期主要再融資操作（MRO）僅借入€180億；相較之下，英格蘭銀行本週短期附買回工具使用額接近紀錄高點£1,320億。市場融資仍比ECB工具便宜，降低銀行例行使用的誘因。

Barclays的Rohan Khanna指出，污名效應也是障礙。ECB公布各國借款金額，某國使用額突然增加，便可能引發外界猜測哪家銀行缺現金，即使資料未公布個別借款銀行。Commerzbank的Christoph Rieger認為，若借款成本降低至更接近現行貨幣市場利率，有助鼓勵銀行常態參與。其他分析師建議更多銀行同時使用，以淡化個別機構借款可能傳遞的訊號。

RBC警告，大量主權債供給可能進一步推升附買回利率，並特別提到法國創紀錄的2027年融資計畫，以及9月底擔保融資市場異常劇烈的變化。Citi的Andrea Appeddu表示，MRO資金需求不足以抵銷超額流動性減少。ECB例行再融資操作因此與傳導保護工具（TPI）的有條件主權債干預同時受到關注，但兩者處理不同問題：銀行以擔保品取得現金的需求，與政府風險溢價擴大的情況，需要不同回應。

歐洲銀行監理方面的評估，稍微緩和市場焦慮。歐洲銀行管理局指出，去年底主權債約占銀行資產13%。監理機關正在加做檢查，但目前認為淨利息收入增加的效益，大致抵銷債券價格下跌的損失。Singular Bank的Roberto Scholtes警告，利率若持續上升，可能增加不良貸款，並拖慢放款及企業金融業務。即時的資產價格衝擊，以及之後對借款人的影響，是同一波緊縮傳導的不同階段。

德國央行執行理事Michael Theurer在週六刊出的訪談中表示，主權危機風險已明顯上升，但尚未見系統性危機，也沒有足以支持ECB干預、根本無法持續的市場趨勢。他呼籲中期財政整頓與有助成長的支出，德國也應如此。

西班牙的新預測顯示，債市單日平靜並未消除通膨問題。西班牙央行將2026年通膨預測上調0.3個百分點至3.9%，2027年預測由2.6%調高至3.7%。能源減稅與交通折扣預計到期，將先推升明年初通膨，之後才放緩。西班牙與歐元區的通膨差距，已從4月的0.5個百分點擴大至9月的1.2個百分點。

成長預測也同步上修，今年為2.6%，2027年為2.2%。住宅仍構成限制：央行估計缺口達75萬戶，2028年可能增至100萬戶；勞工短缺、營建成本與開發障礙限制新增供給。預測呈現經濟活動較強、通膨持續的組合，物價衝擊並非只帶來經濟收縮。

英國房貸市場顯示，央行尚未調整基準利率，市場就可能帶來相當程度的緊縮。英格蘭銀行利率全年維持3.75%，但交換利率上升已把平均房貸利率推向6%。Rightmove資料顯示，9月買家詢問量較去年同期減少9%，每家房仲平均有65戶待售，為逾十年來同期最高。英格蘭銀行8月購屋房貸核准件數降至54,900件，為2023年6月以來最低。

最新波動比較讓傳導問題更鮮明。自伊朗衝突開始，在英鎊交換利率上升的交易日，漲幅中位數約5個基點，高於2022年初以來的3.5個基點；約四分之一的單日漲幅達至少10個基點。放款機構因此更快調整房貸價格，或撤回報價，避免避險成本累積。英國屋主的房貸利率通常只固定兩年或五年，這種波動因而較快傳到需要重新融資的家庭。

## AI募資分化，營收落地與融資能力各受考驗

Firmus Grid週五正式撤回澳洲上市申請，開始向既有投資人尋求$20億至$30億私募融資。知情人士表示，融資可能結合債務與股權，最終規模仍在考慮。原本IPO預計募集約$50億，其中約一半已規劃由既有股東提供，可能有助尋找替代資金。

正式撤回讓先前延後上市的不確定狀態落定。最新營運數據也顯示，公司現況與擬議$300億估值所反映的產能之間仍有距離：截至6月的會計年度營收為$5,100萬，912百萬瓦開發計畫中僅46百萬瓦已建成。所尋求估值約為幾個月前一輪募資的三倍，也超過4月估值的五倍。

UniSuper投資長John Pearce認為，公司業務前景有吸引力，估值卻沒有，並強調未來需要反覆籌措債務與股權資金。Firmus原擬以募資所得，為與DayOne在巴淡島合作開發的計畫購買GPU；該計畫屬於與Nvidia的八年合作。撤回上市因此影響具體建設與設備計畫可取得的資本，也牽涉未來上市估值。

知情人士指出，DayOne仍與銀行初步討論可能發行$5億專案融資債券，由Citi擔任主辦，最快明年可能進入債市。這家新加坡業者已申請在美國IPO，並考慮募集約$50億。即使合作夥伴撤回上市，這些洽談仍在進行。

DayOne已取得大規模銀行融資。一筆總額相當於$70億的貸款中，逾30家放款機構參與其中增額至相當於$37億的部分，分為55億令吉、約合$13億，以及$24億兩部分。公司也正為香港設施尋求HK$18.6億，並於8月為首個新加坡開發案取得四年期S$5.3億貸款。這家亞洲資料中心業者的擴張主要依靠銀行與股權，發債將增加可用的融資管道。

OpenAI的新營收展望，與前一天引發科技股不安的估計有明顯不同。熟悉投資人討論的人士表示，9月底年化營收約$500億，公司預期主要藉由企業業務成長，年底達到或超過$700億。較高的未來營收預期，週五早盤有助緩和AI需求疑慮。

產業的發債負擔仍然龐大。週末公布的最新彙總數據顯示，美國公司今年已發行$1.69兆債券，較去年同期增加約30%；截至週四，平均殖利率上升約1.2個百分點至5.97%。Barclays聯席承銷主管Scott Schulte預期，超大規模雲端業者明年資本支出約$1兆。大型AI借款人在成本上升之際仍維持融資需求，一般企業卻延後交易。

當週發債情況就呈現這種差異。美國企業僅發行$114億，低於交易商預估的$250億至$300億；歐洲發行€162億，甚至不及調查中最低的預測。MUFG的Antoine Baudron表示，多筆交易停滯，因為企業對當前殖利率尚無準備。整體發行放緩，仍與願意付出更高成本建設產能的一批集中融資計畫並存。

軟體業貸款則呈現不同的需求。Proofpoint與Gainwell合計逾$70億貸款，以面額98%出售後，週四報價接近101%；Sophos約$20億美元與歐元貸款，上月以97%發行後，已在面額之上交易。隨AI顛覆業務的疑慮緩和，未參與原始交易的投資人轉向次級市場。週四美國槓桿貸款基金流入$19.3億，為2025年2月5日以來最多，基準利率上升帶來的浮動利率收益吸引買家。

體質最弱的借款人則朝相反方向走。JPMorgan最新資料顯示，交易價格低於面額60%的貸款，由$400億增至$650億，為2020年3月以來最大的重度困境貸款規模。Beach Point的Sinjin Bowron認為，軟體業被顛覆的疑慮只是暫緩，並未消失；他也指出，貸款文件保障變得更嚴密，是特定貸款更具吸引力的原因。剛完成條款修訂的交易在次級市場漲價，仍可能與困境貸款增加同時發生。

Deutsche Bank的George Saravelos提出另一項風險，方向與當前偏空債市的主流論述相反。他認為，AI企業IPO失敗、營收不如預期或安全事件，可能引發美元下跌、債券上漲的反轉，而集中度使市場低估這種可能性。這為當前融資壓力提供具體的替代情境：投資與借款今日支撐名目成長，若市場失去對預期回報的信心，資金需求與風險偏好卻可能同時驟降。

## 電信債困境與債權保障，拉開企業債表現差距

Virgin Media O2於2033年7月到期的供應商融資債券，週五最多下跌5.3歐分至每€1面額37.7歐分，約為7月初價值的一半。Nexfibre收購Netomnia受到監管審查，威脅這筆原預計帶來約£10億現金、協助降槓桿的交易。Bloomberg Intelligence分析師Erhan Gurses估計，交易完全遭否決的機率為40%，另有60%機率附帶嚴格定價與投資補救要求獲准，從而削弱效益。

週四倫敦槓桿融資會議上，投資人向共同持有人Liberty Global追問可能採取債務管理交易的情況。主管表示尚未做這些決策，並強調維持資本市場融資能力與降低槓桿。Virgin Media表示，Liberty與Telefónica兩大股東都持續支持業務，2029年前沒有債務到期。

公司財務規模使監管決定格外重要。Virgin Media淨負債約£220億，6月底槓桿約為年化調整後獲利的5.9倍，每年營運與資本支出約£80億。Gurses估計，Netomnia交易可使槓桿降低0.25倍。討論中的措施包括削減成本、調整資本支出，以及原先預期的£2億股東股息，若收購失敗尤其需要考慮。法定競爭審查決策期限為12月15日；管理層預期2026年調整後獲利下降3%至5%。

美國電信債週五面臨另一種威脅。紐約時間上午10:30，Verizon於2058年到期、票息6.05%的債券，相對美國公債利差擴大22個基點至220個基點；交易較清淡的AT&T債券，利差最多擴大6個基點。此前SpaceX宣布向Grain Management收購頻譜，以支援室內衛星直連手機服務。AT&T與Verizon分別是Bloomberg高評級美元債指數中，非金融債務規模第三與第四大的發行人。

SpaceX要將衛星服務與地面網路結合，仍需FCC批准。Bloomberg Intelligence的Stephen Flynn認為，SpaceX的募資能力提高了既有無線電信業者面臨重大競爭的可能性。這些個別債券的利差擴大源於新競爭者，週五收盤美國整體高收益債利差則小幅收窄。

Electronic Arts（EA）與債權人對控制權變更付款的爭議，新增一項評等論點。公司告知債權人，部分債券已取得Egan-Jones投資等級評等，並認為可替代Moody's撤回的評等。由Akin Gump與Houlihan Lokey提供顧問服務的債權人反對，主張私人替代評等不能取代公開評等，且文件禁止在程序進行中變更。受託人U.S. Bank其後通知公司將辭任，原因是9月8日違約通知造成利益衝突。

爭議涉及EA在$550億收購案後，以美國公債作為擔保品解除債務義務的做法。若避開控制權變更付款，可節省約$2.5億。2031年到期、票息1.85%的債券持有人獲提議以面額約92%處理，2051年到期、票息2.95%的持有人則約74%，相較一般控制權變更付款為101%。核心問題包括：這項保障究竟是可透過債務解除程序消滅的契約條款，還是仍須履行的付款義務；以及新評等是否符合文件要求。EA反對債權人的違約主張。

評等較佳的企業仍順利完成發行。PepsiCo在下修獲利展望隔天，於週五募集€10億，三年與九年期債券各占一半。短天期券相對交換利率中間價的定價利差為33個基點，初步討論約60個基點；長天期券為73個基點，先前討論約105個基點。儘管北美飲料銷量今年下降3%，預期A1/A+評等仍使這筆交易與困境借款人有所區別。

併購與私人信貸市場也在籌備大型交易。Siemens Energy蒸汽渦輪業務可能出售多數股權，銀行正提議€60億至€70億融資額度。預計動用的貸款與高收益債合計約€45億至€50億，另有約€10億循環額度與€15億保證額度。以約€9億獲利計算，擬議槓桿約5倍；Siemens打算保留相當比例的少數股權。

法國教育業者Omnes正尋求為約€7億債務再融資，主要是2028年4月到期的銀行借款；另有€2.16億可轉換債於2029年4月到期，年度獲利約€9,500萬。公司業務受政府支持的學徒培訓經費影響，再融資將近之際，公共支出削減與利息費用上升形成雙重壓力。現有放款人包括Goldman Sachs、PSP Investments、M&G與Clearlake Credit。

## 亞洲流動性措施與其他融資市場

印度央行週五把吸收剩餘資金的原則性承諾，轉為具體操作。RBI宣布週一出售2,500億盧比的六檔債券，剩餘期限四至八年；並自10月16日起，將法定現金準備金每日最低維持比例由90%調高至99%。過剩流動性從9月創紀錄的11兆盧比，降至七週低點3.6兆盧比。

ICICI Securities Primary Dealership經濟學家Abhishek Upadhyay預期，新增供給將使週一殖利率上升約5個基點，部分原因是投資人會預期後續仍有售債。他認為準備金維持比例調整只會讓隔夜利率小幅上升，在剩餘流動性仍龐大時，利率仍將低於附買回政策利率。這項預測區分了兩種影響：在供給已多的公債市場出售債券所帶來的利率風險，與隔夜資金供應收緊。

日本8月家庭支出較去年同期下降3.1%，小於預期的3.6%降幅，但已連續第九個月萎縮；季節調整後月增僅0.1%。教育、食品、住宅維護、租金與水電支出都減少，交通與通訊是唯一未下降的項目。S&P Global Market Intelligence的Harumi Taguchi強調，日益增加的退休人口無法受惠於薪資上升，這有助解釋薪資改善為何尚未帶動更廣泛的支出復甦。

中國週五核准額外5,500億元人民幣的省級結轉債券額度，高於原先預期約5,000億元。一般債額度3,000億元將協助縣級政府支付日常支出；2,500億元專項債額度則用於10月至12月實際專案需求，優先分配給實力較強的省份。北京追求4.5%至5%的成長目標之際，這項配置既緩解地方現金壓力，也將投資借款限定於專案。Standard Chartered的丁爽認為，投資的主要限制是預算執行緩慢，而非融資能力不足。

中國借款成本低，也吸引外國發行人進入人民幣債市。Bloomberg最新彙整顯示，今年發行的熊貓債中，逾40%獲准將募集資金用於境外，金額最高達1,300億元人民幣。截至10月8日，外國借款人募集1,155億元人民幣，為去年全年總額的兩倍，占市場47%，高於三年前的13%。離岸點心債發行達1兆元人民幣，非中國發行人占比由23%升至35%。

成本節省取決於資金用途。UBS在8月以1.78%發行五年期熊貓債，但將人民幣借款避險轉為其他幣別，成本約3%，會削弱大部分優勢。若借款用於人民幣計價貿易，就能避開換匯成本。上半年中國貨品貿易中，29%以人民幣結算，比去年同期多1個百分點，讓人民幣負債的自然用途持續增加。

菲律賓宣布自1月4日起實施債市准入改革。在計畫納入JPMorgan新興市場指數前，披索債券交割計算將取消對溢價與折價的稅務調整，使定價符合國際慣例。溢價債持有人可能產生交割收益，折價債持有人可能產生損失，持有至到期者則不受實際影響。契約利息與本金付款維持原狀，20%的利息所得稅也不變。外資持有約4%的菲律賓政府證券，相較印尼為13%、馬來西亞為21%。

烏茲別克最大私人本國企業債發行人Uzum，考慮最快年底或2027年初首次發行歐洲債券，為無擔保放款成長籌資。自2025年起，公司已發行2.1兆索姆本地債券，本月又將歐亞開發銀行融資由$7,000萬提高至$1億。該區企業已吸引大量認購訂單，Uzum潛在國際借款為區域增加另一項資金需求。

委內瑞拉債權人則在強化談判地位。臨時債權人團體目前掌握約37%未償債務，名目金額至少$220億，並預期未來幾週提高至40%。2027年到期債券全週上漲約4美分，投資人會議重燃重整樂觀情緒，收復9月下旬以來跌幅。TCW的David Robbins預期回收率約為面額的55%或更高。EMFI的Guillermo Guerrero提到尚未證實的市場傳聞，指IMF可能只提供建議，而不主導債務可持續性分析，或使協議條件更寬鬆；IMF的角色與回收條款都尚未確定。

## 後續市場觀察

美國現券債市10月12日週一休市，股市仍開市。主要通膨考驗隨後在10月14日週三紐約時間上午8:30登場：9月CPI預期月增0.6%，前值0.4%；核心CPI預期月增0.2%，前值0.3%。Bloomberg調查的年增率預估分別為3.6%與2.5%。若整體通膨由汽油帶動加速、基礎物價漲幅卻放緩，帶來的政策問題將不同於價格壓力廣泛傳到商品與服務，尤其密西根調查已顯示通膨預期提高。

數據公布後、週六靜默期開始前，聯準會官員將陸續發言。Kevin Warsh週四在曼谷IMF會議發表談話；Christopher Waller與Beth Hammack也有排定公開活動，Hammack的時間為週一紐約時間下午12:50。交易員仍預期12月升息，週五美國公債市場報導則顯示，10月升息機率約20%。眼前重點在於通膨細節會否改變緊縮速度，或較高的市場借貸成本能否讓聯準會繼續耐心等待。

週二NFIB樂觀指數預期為98，前值98.7；成屋銷售預期396萬戶，前值398萬戶。週四的零售銷售、失業救濟申請與生產者物價，將擴大對需求及物價傳導的觀察。當前景氣評估剛降至歷史低點，家庭信心疲弱與實際支出的差異仍有重要意義。

週末能源風險進一步發展。週日報導指出，利雅德哈立德國王機場再次遇襲，此前週六攻擊造成12人死亡；達曼法赫德國王機場也遭攻擊。BP與Shell高層退出世界石油大會，利雅德金融區延長遠距辦公。川普表示，烏克蘭與俄羅斯已同意能源停火；澤倫斯基則表示支持能源停火，莫斯科也必須採取相同行動。這些晚於週五布蘭特收在$104.72的發展，構成重新開市的風險背景；實際燃料與運輸狀況仍決定多少舒緩能傳到通膨。

歐洲將面臨供給考驗，法國週四最多發行€120億中期債券。Lagarde週三在曼谷的公開活動，可能談及市場動盪與政策傳導；匈牙利預算草案則將把Peter Magyar的財政整頓承諾轉成具體數字。他最新詳述的財富稅，對超過10億福林的部分課1%、超過1,000億福林的部分課1.5%，預期每年收入2,000億福林，同時還需支應額外5,000億福林醫療支出。目標仍是2030年赤字降至GDP的3%，相較今年估計7.5%。

企業供給預期在清淡的一週後回升。交易商預估美國高評級債發行約$300億，主要來自公布財報後的銀行借款；歐洲調查近80%的受訪者預期發行超過€300億。AI借款人持續推進融資計畫之際，實際定價與完成發行的情況，將顯示具吸引力的殖利率是否能帶來足夠資金。Firmus替代融資、DayOne拓展新管道，以及Virgin Media降槓桿的選擇，各自考驗這種融資能力。

overall_summary.headline: 家庭通膨預期上升，美國公債回跌、曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
10月9日，家庭通膨預期提高、能源價格居高不下，使聯準會進一步升息的可能性持續牽動市場，美國公債回吐部分由標售帶動的漲幅。2年期殖利率上升2.92個基點至4.7869%，10年期上升1.1個基點至5.2378%，30年期則下降0.45個基點至5.5956%。2年與10年期利差縮小1.82個基點至45.09個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.23個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降1.13個基點，顯示當日殖利率升幅來自扣除通膨後的融資成本。各基準殖利率全週仍然下降。

密西根大學初步信心指數降至46.3，現況評估創歷史新低；較短期通膨預期升至4.7%，5年期升至3.5%。布蘭特原油盤中曾回落，仍收在$104.72。股市回升，美國高收益債與強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債利差收窄，但最新部位資料顯示，資產管理機構正在削減超長天期美國公債期貨曝險。

歐洲主權債穩定，超額準備金減少、銀行不願使用ECB再融資工具，使融資壓力持續受到關注。企業取得資金的情況仍不均：Firmus撤回澳洲上市，尋求$20億至$30億私募融資；DayOne持續初步洽談發債；Virgin Media O2原預期有助降槓桿的交易受到監管審查，債券價格下跌。高殖利率仍吸引買家，現金創造能力與契約保障卻讓借款人表現分化。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries gave back part of their auction-led recovery on October 9 as expensive energy and rising household inflation expectations kept further Federal Reserve tightening in view. Selling concentrated in shorter and intermediate maturities: the two-year yield rose 2.92 basis points to 4.7869%, while the 10-year increased 1.1 basis points to 5.2378%. The 30-year held its ground, slipping 0.45 basis point to 5.5956%, leaving a flatter curve rather than a renewed, uniform long-bond rout.

The preliminary Michigan survey supplied the day's clearest economic development. Consumer sentiment fell more than expected, assessments of current conditions reached a record low, and inflation expectations increased at both reported horizons. That combination kept the pressure on households visible without offering a straightforward disinflationary signal. Brent finished at $104.72 a barrel, up 0.42%, despite earlier diplomatic and supply-related relief.

The broader market absorbed the session more comfortably. U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably, while equities recovered. Yet new positioning figures showed long-duration futures exposure being cut, European sovereign volatility was drawing attention to the ECB's regular liquidity facilities, and corporate financing remained sharply differentiated. Firmus formally abandoned its Australian listing and sought private capital; DayOne continued preliminary bond discussions; Virgin Media O2's debt fell further as a threatened asset transaction complicated deleveraging. High absolute yields were attracting buyers, but access to capital increasingly depended on the borrower, its cash generation and its contractual protections.

## Household Inflation Expectations Rise as the Treasury Curve Flattens

Friday's Treasury losses were smaller than the previous session's gains and left benchmark yields lower over the week. The five-year rose 2.68 basis points to 5.0157%, joining the two-year as the weaker part of the curve. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1.82 basis points to 45.09, while 2s30s contracted 3.37 to 80.87. The longest maturity retained support after the week's successful auctions, even as the securities more exposed to the policy outlook moved lower.

Over the week, two-year yields fell 4.01 basis points, five-year yields 3.83, 10-year yields 3.52 and 30-year yields 2.54. Those declines offered a modest respite from a much larger monthly repricing. The 10-year remained 44.78 basis points above its month-earlier level and the 30-year 34.96 higher; the two-year's 39.19-basis-point increase showed that the pressure extended well beyond long-end supply and fiscal concerns.

At 10 years, Friday's increase was in real yields. The TIPS yield rose 2.23 basis points to 2.8851%, while breakeven inflation declined 1.13 basis points to 2.3527%. Over the month, real yields had increased 47.01 basis points and breakevens had fallen 2.23. Energy remained central to the policy debate, but the daily market decomposition showed higher inflation-adjusted financing costs alongside lower longer-term inflation compensation.

Michigan's preliminary October sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, below the 47.6 consensus. The current-conditions measure dropped to 44.7 from 50.9, reaching an all-time low as gasoline prices, borrowing costs and slower hiring weighed on households. Expectations about the economy improved to 47.3 from 46.3, so the deterioration was concentrated in the assessment of present conditions rather than spread evenly across the survey.

Inflation expectations moved in the other direction. The survey's nearer-horizon measure increased to 4.7% from 4.6%, and its five-year measure rose to 3.5% from 3.4%. Views of buying conditions for durable goods also reached a record low, according to Bloomberg's account. Consumers were reporting both reduced affordability and greater expected price pressure, a mix that complicates the choice between further inflation restraint and allowing the recent rise in market rates to work through demand.

The Fed's Survey of Consumer Finances, released Friday, added a different, longer-period observation about household resilience. In the three years through 2025, median net worth rose 2% to $215,900, while average net worth rose 7% to $1,241,500. Income inequality narrowed as lower-income families received modest pay gains and incomes at the top declined, but the top 10% of earners still held more than 50 times the average wealth of the bottom 20%.

Stock ownership fell to 56% of families from 58% between 2022 and 2025, even as the S&P 500 rose nearly 80% over that period. Families in the bottom half of the income distribution accounted for almost all the decline in participation. The share of families with debt stayed at 77%, but 8.6% had debt-payment-to-income ratios above 40%, the highest proportion since 2010. The historical survey helps explain why strong equity markets and weak household confidence can coexist: asset gains are unevenly distributed, while financing expenses draw on current income.

Friday's risk-asset recovery nevertheless showed continued confidence in corporate earnings. The S&P 500 gained 0.59% to 7,811.54 and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.51%, although semiconductor shares lost another 0.41%. The VIX fell to 14.84. Bloomberg's market account put barely a third of S&P 500 constituents above their 50-day moving averages and just 27% of Russell 2000 members above that threshold. The large indexes' resilience therefore coexisted with weakness among smaller and more rate-sensitive businesses.

The dollar strengthened modestly, with the Dollar Index up 0.07% to 102.21. Separately, the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index completed a fourth weekly advance, gaining about 3% over that period, its longest winning streak since early 2025. CFTC figures through October 6 showed more than $35 billion in bullish dollar wagers. CIBC's Sarah Ying attributed demand to risk aversion, European fiscal concerns and threatened Strait of Hormuz supply, while PGIM's Robert Tipp emphasized the United States' relative capacity to sustain higher rates.

New research and positioning evidence also put the recent Treasury move in a broader setting. The New York Fed's term-premium model showed an increase of around 40 basis points since mid-September to roughly 0.98%, the highest since 2014, more than accounting for the nearly 30-basis-point rise in 10-year yields over that particular interval. A separate estimate incorporating economists' policy forecasts reached 1.08%, its highest since 2010. These are model estimates of compensation for holding duration, with Barclays researchers identifying macro uncertainty, changing stock-bond correlations, debt supply and fiscal concerns as possible contributors.

Friday's CFTC release supplied a more concrete measure of exposure reduction. Asset managers cut their bullish ultra-long Treasury futures position by about $27 million per basis point of risk in the two weeks ended October 6, equivalent to roughly $38 billion of the current 10-year cash note. Bloomberg's account linked the selling to changes in the cheapest-to-deliver securities that extended portfolio duration. Ultra-long futures open interest had declined for seven consecutive sessions, removing almost $20 million per basis point of risk. The observations concern positions and earlier trading, while explaining why technical selling could reinforce a fundamental repricing of long bonds.

Citi offered a prospective supply response in a late-Friday note. U.S. rates strategist Jason Williams expects the Treasury to cut 20- and 30-year auction sizes by $3 billion each at the November 4 refunding announcement, replacing the funding with more bills. He also raised the possibility of cancelling 20-year sales. His argument concerned pension demand potentially shifting toward long-dated, high-quality technology debt; he did not attribute the overall level of rates to that corporate issuance. The forecast adds a specific proposed scale to the debate over Treasury maturities, with an October 16 dealer questionnaire potentially revealing the department's interest in the issue.

## Europe Finds Price Relief but Faces a Funding Constraint

European government bonds stabilized Friday as oil retreated earlier in the session and French political news quietened. France's 10-year premium over Germany narrowed 3 basis points to 137 in Bloomberg's trading account; a separate intraday observation put it as low as 135. French yields fell 3 basis points to 4.86%. The recovery brought French bonds toward their first weekly gain in six weeks and Italian debt toward its first in nine.

Relative pricing still distinguished France from its neighbors. The French-Italian 10-year yield gap reached 30 basis points Friday, a record since the euro's creation, even while the broader market recovered. Aegon's Irina Kurochkina said investors were using the recent widening to buy Italy and Spain but largely avoiding France. Jefferies' Mohit Kumar described a potential buyer strike rather than a sovereign restructuring crisis and expected hedge funds to add shorts into rallies. His view that intervention beyond words would require a French-German spread around 200 basis points was a strategist's assessment of the ECB's likely response.

The liquidity debate extended beyond sovereign credit. Euro-area excess reserves have declined toward €2 trillion from more than €4.5 trillion four years ago, and repo rates have reached their highest since March 2025. Banks borrowed only €18 billion in the ECB's one-week Main Refinancing Operations, against a near-record £132 billion in the Bank of England's Short-Term Repo this week. Market financing remains cheaper than the ECB facility, limiting the incentive to use it routinely.

Barclays' Rohan Khanna identified stigma as another obstacle. The ECB publishes borrowing by country, allowing a sudden increase in one national total to trigger speculation about which bank needs cash even though individual borrowers are not named. Commerzbank's Christoph Rieger argued that cheaper access, closer to prevailing money-market rates, would help encourage regular participation. Other analysts proposed broader simultaneous use by banks to dilute the signal associated with any individual institution.

RBC warned that heavy sovereign supply could push repo rates higher still, highlighting France's record 2027 funding plan and an unusually sharp end-September secured-funding move. Citi's Andrea Appeddu said demand for MRO cash was not sufficient to offset falling excess liquidity. That places the ECB's routine refinancing operations alongside, but distinct from, the conditional sovereign-bond intervention available through its Transmission Protection Instrument. A bank's need for cash against collateral and a government's widening risk premium require different responses.

European bank supervision offered a qualified counterweight to market anxiety. Sovereign bonds represented about 13% of bank assets at the end of last year, according to the European Banking Authority. Supervisors are making additional checks, but currently judge the benefits to net interest income to be largely offsetting losses from falling bond prices. Singular Bank's Roberto Scholtes warned that a sustained increase in rates could raise nonperforming loans and slow lending and corporate banking. The immediate asset-price shock and its eventual effect on borrowers remain different stages of the same tightening.

In comments published Saturday, Bundesbank Executive Board member Michael Theurer said sovereign-crisis risks had risen significantly, while finding no systemic crisis or fundamentally unsustainable market trend warranting ECB intervention. He called for medium-term fiscal consolidation and growth-enhancing expenditure, including in Germany. His assessment reinforced the distinction between acknowledging rising fiscal risks and treating the recent volatility as grounds for central-bank purchases.

Spain's new forecasts illustrated why a calmer bond session did not remove the inflation problem. The Bank of Spain raised its 2026 inflation projection by 0.3 percentage point to 3.9%, and lifted its 2027 estimate to 3.7% from 2.6%. The expected expiry of energy tax cuts and transport discounts would raise inflation early next year before it slowed. Spain's inflation differential against the euro area had widened to 1.2 percentage points in September from 0.5 in April.

Growth forecasts rose as well, to 2.6% this year and 2.2% in 2027. Housing remained a constraint: the central bank estimated a shortage of 750,000 homes, potentially reaching 1 million by 2028, with labor shortages, construction costs and development obstacles limiting new supply. The forecast combines stronger activity with persistent inflation, rather than describing the price shock as a purely contractionary force.

Britain's mortgage market showed how much restraint can arrive before a central bank changes its benchmark. With the BOE rate held at 3.75% all year, rising swaps had pushed average mortgage rates toward 6%. Rightmove reported September buyer inquiries 9% below a year earlier and 65 properties for sale per estate agent, the highest seasonal figure in more than a decade. BOE approvals for house purchases fell to 54,900 in August, their lowest since June 2023.

New volatility comparisons sharpened the transmission problem. Since the Iran conflict began, the median increase in sterling swaps on rising-rate days has been around 5 basis points, against 3.5 since the start of 2022; roughly a quarter of those daily increases reached at least 10 basis points. Lenders were repricing faster or withdrawing offers to avoid accumulating hedge costs. Because British homeowners commonly fix for only two or five years, that volatility reaches refinancing households relatively quickly.

## AI Capital Raising Splits Between Revenue Delivery and Funding Access

Firmus Grid formally withdrew its Australian listing application Friday and began exploring $2 billion to $3 billion of private financing from existing investors. People familiar with the discussions said the structure could mix debt and equity, with the final size still under consideration. Existing shareholders had already planned to supply roughly half the approximately $5 billion sought in the IPO, potentially easing the search for replacement capital.

The completed withdrawal resolved the earlier uncertainty over postponement. Fresh operating detail showed the distance between Firmus's business today and the capacity embedded in its proposed $30 billion valuation: it generated $51 million of revenue in the financial year through June, and only 46 megawatts of a 912-megawatt development pipeline had been built. The valuation sought was about triple that of a funding round a few months earlier and more than five times the April valuation.

UniSuper investment chief John Pearce said the business story was compelling but the valuation was not, and highlighted the need for repeated debt and equity raising. Firmus's proposed proceeds would have financed GPUs for the Batam project it is developing with DayOne under an eight-year Nvidia partnership. Its withdrawal thus affects the capital available for a defined construction and equipment program, not only the valuation of an eventual stock-market debut.

DayOne continued preliminary discussions with banks over a potential $500 million project-financing bond, with Citi as lead arranger and market access possible as early as next year, according to people familiar with the plans. The Singapore-based operator has filed for a U.S. IPO and has been considering raising around $5 billion. Those discussions remained active despite its partner's withdrawal.

Its borrowing already reaches substantial bank capacity. More than 30 lenders participated in an upsized $3.7 billion-equivalent portion of a broader $7 billion-equivalent loan, split between 5.5 billion ringgit, or $1.3 billion, and $2.4 billion. DayOne is also seeking HK$1.86 billion for a Hong Kong facility and obtained a four-year S$530 million loan in August for its first Singapore development. A bond would widen the financing channels available to an Asian data-center operator whose expansion has principally drawn on banks and equity.

OpenAI supplied a materially different revenue outlook from the estimate that had unsettled technology shares the previous day. People familiar with investor discussions said annualized revenue was roughly $50 billion at the end of September, with the company expecting to reach or exceed $70 billion by year-end, largely through enterprise growth. The distinction is between the September run rate and a later target, rather than competing descriptions of the same observation. The higher forward expectation helped ease concerns about AI demand early Friday.

The industry's issuance burden nevertheless remained substantial. New aggregate figures published over the weekend showed $1.69 trillion of U.S. corporate bonds sold this year, about 30% more than a year earlier, while average yields had risen approximately 1.2 percentage points to 5.97% as of Thursday. Barclays syndicate co-head Scott Schulte expects hyperscaler capital expenditure around $1 trillion next year. The financing appetite of large AI borrowers was persisting through higher costs even as conventional issuers postponed transactions.

That difference was visible in weekly issuance. U.S. corporations sold only $11.4 billion, against dealers' expectation of $25 billion to $30 billion, and European sales of €16.2 billion fell below even the lowest surveyed forecasts. MUFG's Antoine Baudron said several transactions had stalled because companies were unprepared for current yields. The aggregate slowdown therefore coexisted with a concentrated pipeline from borrowers willing to pay more to build capacity.

Software loans provided a contrasting form of demand. Proofpoint and Gainwell loans totaling more than $7 billion were quoted near 101 cents on the dollar Thursday after being sold at 98, while roughly $2 billion of Sophos dollar and euro loans traded above par after issuance at 97 last month. Investors who missed the original deals were entering through the secondary market as fears about AI disruption eased. U.S. leveraged-loan funds received $1.93 billion Thursday, their largest inflow since February 5, 2025, with floating-rate income drawing buyers as benchmark rates rose.

The weakest borrowers were moving in the opposite direction. JPMorgan's latest figures put loans trading below 60 cents at $65 billion, up from $40 billion and the largest deeply distressed pool since March 2020. Beach Point's Sinjin Bowron regarded software's disruption concerns as paused rather than eliminated, while pointing to tighter documentation as a reason particular loans had become attractive. A stronger secondary price for a newly amended transaction can coexist with a growing distressed tail.

Deutsche Bank's George Saravelos identified the opposite risk to the prevailing bearish bond narrative. He argued that a failed AI IPO, disappointing revenues or a safety event could trigger a dollar-negative, bond-positive reversal, and that concentration made this possibility underpriced. His assessment puts a specific alternative alongside the current financing pressure: investment and borrowing can support nominal growth today, while a loss of confidence in the expected payoff could abruptly reduce both capital demand and risk appetite.

## Telecom Distress and Creditor Rights Differentiate Corporate Debt

Virgin Media O2's July 2033 vendor-financing note fell as much as 5.3 cents Friday to 37.7 cents on the euro, roughly half its early-July value. Regulatory scrutiny of Nexfibre's purchase of Netomnia threatened a transaction expected to produce about £1 billion of cash toward deleveraging. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Erhan Gurses estimated a 40% chance of an outright block and a 60% chance of approval with strict pricing and investment remedies that would dilute its benefits.

At Thursday's London leveraged-finance conference, investors pressed co-owner Liberty Global over the possibility of a liability-management exercise. Executives said they were not yet making those decisions and emphasized preserving capital-market access and reducing leverage. Virgin Media said both owners, Liberty and Telefónica, were committed to the business, with no debt falling due until 2029.

The financial scale makes the regulatory decision consequential. Virgin Media had roughly £22 billion of net debt, leverage of about 5.9 times annualized adjusted earnings at end-June and annual operating and capital spending around £8 billion. The Netomnia transaction would reduce leverage by 0.25 times, according to Gurses. Cost cuts, changes to capital spending and a previously expected £200 million shareholder dividend were among the measures discussed, particularly if the acquisition failed. The statutory competition decision deadline is December 15, while management expects 2026 adjusted earnings to fall 3%-5%.

U.S. telecom debt faced a different threat Friday. Verizon's 6.05% note due in 2058 widened 22 basis points to 220 over Treasuries at 10:30 a.m. New York time, and AT&T bonds widened as much as 6 basis points in lighter trading. The move followed SpaceX's announced purchase of spectrum from Grain Management that would support indoor satellite-to-cell service. AT&T and Verizon are respectively the third- and fourth-largest nonfinancial debt constituents of Bloomberg's high-grade dollar index.

FCC approval remains necessary before SpaceX combines its satellite service with a terrestrial network. Bloomberg Intelligence's Stephen Flynn said its capital-raising ability increased the prospect of significant competition for the established wireless operators. These were instrument-specific spread losses tied to an emerging competitor, while broad U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly at Friday's close.

Electronic Arts added a new ratings argument to its dispute with bondholders over change-of-control payments. The company told creditors it had obtained an investment-grade Egan-Jones rating for some bonds and regarded it as a substitute for Moody's withdrawn rating. Creditors advised by Akin Gump and Houlihan Lokey contested that substitution, arguing that a private alternative could not replace the public rating and that the documents prohibited a change mid-process. Trustee U.S. Bank subsequently notified the company it would resign because the September 8 default notice created conflicts of interest.

The disagreement turns on EA's use of Treasury collateral to defease the obligations after its $55 billion buyout. Avoiding the change-of-control payment could save roughly $250 million. Holders of 1.85% notes due in 2031 had been offered about 92 cents and owners of 2.95% notes due in 2051 about 74, versus the usual 101-cent change-of-control payment. The central question is whether the protection is a covenant extinguished by defeasance or a payment obligation that survives, alongside whether the new rating satisfies the documents. EA disputes the creditors' default claim.

Better-rated issuance continued to clear. PepsiCo raised €1 billion Friday, divided equally between three- and nine-year notes, a day after lowering its profit outlook. The shorter tranche priced at 33 basis points over mid-swaps after initial discussions around 60; the longer priced at 73 after talks around 105. Expected A1/A+ ratings helped distinguish the transaction from distressed borrowers, despite North American beverage volumes falling 3% this year.

Acquisition and private-credit markets were also preparing substantial transactions. Banks were pitching €6 billion to €7 billion of facilities for a potential majority sale of Siemens Energy's steam-turbine business. Drawn loans and high-yield bonds would total roughly €4.5 billion to €5 billion, alongside about €1 billion of revolving capacity and €1.5 billion of guarantees. The prospective leverage was around 5 times against approximately €900 million of earnings, with Siemens intending to retain a meaningful minority stake.

French education operator Omnes was seeking to refinance around €700 million of debt, mainly bank borrowing due in April 2028. It also reported €216 million of convertibles due in April 2029, while annual earnings were about €95 million. Its exposure to state-backed apprenticeship funding places public spending cuts beside higher interest expense as the refinancing approaches. Existing lenders include Goldman Sachs, PSP Investments, M&G and Clearlake Credit.

## Asian Liquidity Measures and Alternative Funding Markets

India's central bank moved from a general commitment to absorb surplus cash to specific operations Friday. The RBI announced a 250 billion-rupee sale of six bonds maturing in four to eight years for Monday and raised the daily minimum for maintaining required cash reserves to 99% from 90%, effective October 16. Excess liquidity had fallen to 3.6 trillion rupees, a seven-week low, from September's 11 trillion record.

ICICI Securities Primary Dealership economist Abhishek Upadhyay expected the additional supply to lift yields by about 5 basis points Monday, partly because investors would anticipate further sales. He thought the reserve-maintenance change would raise overnight rates only marginally, leaving them below the repo rate while the surplus remained large. The forecast distinguishes selling duration into a heavily supplied government market from tightening the availability of overnight cash.

Japan's August household spending fell 3.1% from a year earlier, less than the forecast 3.6% decline but extending the contraction to a ninth month. Seasonally adjusted spending rose just 0.1% on the month. Education, food, home maintenance, rents and utilities weakened, while transportation and communications was the only component to avoid a decline. S&P Global Market Intelligence's Harumi Taguchi emphasized that a growing retired population does not benefit from wage increases, helping explain why improving pay had not produced a broader spending recovery.

China authorized an additional 550 billion yuan of carry-over provincial bond quotas Friday, above the roughly 500 billion expected. General borrowing of 300 billion yuan would help county governments meet everyday spending needs; 250 billion of special-bond capacity was directed toward actual project needs in October-December, with stronger provinces favored. The allocation both addressed local cash strain and constrained investment borrowing to projects, as Beijing sought its 4.5%-5% growth target. Standard Chartered's Ding Shuang argued that slow budget execution, rather than inadequate financing capacity, had been the main restraint on investment.

China's low borrowing costs were meanwhile drawing foreign issuers into yuan debt. Bloomberg's new compilation showed regulators permitting offshore use of proceeds from more than 40% of panda bonds sold this year, as much as 130 billion yuan. Foreign borrowers raised 115.5 billion yuan through October 8, twice last year's total, and represented 47% of the market against 13% three years ago. Offshore dim-sum issuance reached 1 trillion yuan, with non-Chinese issuers' share rising to 35% from 23%.

The savings depend on the use of proceeds. UBS issued a five-year panda bond at 1.78% in August, but hedging yuan borrowing into another currency costs about 3%, eroding much of the advantage. Borrowers financing yuan-denominated trade can avoid that conversion cost. The currency settled 29% of China's goods trade in the first half, one percentage point more than a year earlier, creating a growing natural use for yuan liabilities.

The Philippines announced a market-access reform effective January 4. It will remove tax adjustments on premiums and discounts from peso-bond settlement calculations, aligning pricing with international conventions before planned inclusion in JPMorgan's emerging-market index. Premium-bond holders may realize settlement gains and discount-bond holders losses, while investors holding to maturity face no actual impact. Contractual interest and principal payments remain intact, and the 20% interest-income tax is unchanged. Foreign investors hold about 4% of government securities, compared with 13% in Indonesia and 21% in Malaysia.

Uzum, Uzbekistan's largest private domestic corporate issuer, was considering its first eurobond as early as year-end or early 2027 to fund unsecured-lending growth. It has sold 2.1 trillion soums of local notes since 2025 and this month increased Eurasian Development Bank financing to $100 million from $70 million. Its prospective international borrowing adds a different source of funding demand to a region where companies have attracted large order books.

Venezuela's creditors were strengthening their negotiating position. The ad-hoc group now controlled about 37% of outstanding debt, at least $22 billion in nominal value, and expected to reach 40% in coming weeks. Notes due in 2027 gained about 4 cents over the week, reversing their losses since late September as investor meetings renewed optimism about restructuring. TCW's David Robbins envisaged recoveries in the mid-50s or higher. EMFI's Guillermo Guerrero described unconfirmed market rumors that the IMF would advise rather than own the debt-sustainability analysis, potentially allowing a softer agreement; neither the institutional role nor recovery terms had been settled.

## Forward Market Significance

U.S. cash bond trading is closed Monday, October 12, while equities remain open. The main inflation test follows Wednesday, October 14, at 8:30 a.m. New York time: September CPI is expected to rise 0.6% month on month after 0.4%, while core CPI is expected at 0.2% after 0.3%. Bloomberg's survey puts the annual rates at 3.6% and 2.5%, respectively. A gasoline-led headline acceleration alongside slower underlying prices would leave a different policy question from broad pass-through into goods and services, especially after Michigan's higher inflation expectations.

Fed communications follow that release before the blackout begins Saturday. Kevin Warsh speaks Thursday at the IMF meetings in Bangkok; Christopher Waller and Beth Hammack also have scheduled appearances, with Hammack due Monday at 12:50 p.m. New York time. Traders continued to expect a December increase, while Friday's Treasury account assigned about a 20% chance to an October move. The immediate issue is whether the inflation detail changes the pace of tightening or whether higher market borrowing costs allow continued patience.

Tuesday's NFIB optimism reading is expected at 98 after 98.7, and existing-home sales at 3.96 million after 3.98 million. Retail sales, claims and producer prices on Thursday will broaden the assessment of demand and price transmission. These releases arrive after a record-low current-conditions assessment, with the distinction between weak household confidence and realized spending still consequential.

Energy risks developed further over the weekend. A Sunday account reported another attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport after a Saturday strike killed 12 people, and an attack on King Fahd airport in Dammam. BP and Shell executives withdrew from the World Petroleum Congress, while Riyadh's financial district extended remote working. Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire; Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he supported one and that Moscow must do the same. These later developments set the risk backdrop for reopening after Friday's $104.72 Brent close, with physical fuel and transport conditions still determining how much relief reaches inflation.

Europe faces an upcoming supply test as France offers up to €12 billion of medium-term bonds Thursday. Lagarde's Wednesday appearances in Bangkok can address market turbulence and policy transmission, while Hungary's draft budget will turn Peter Magyar's consolidation promises into fiscal numbers. His newly detailed wealth tax would levy 1% above 1 billion forint and 1.5% above 100 billion, with expected annual revenue of 200 billion forint; that must coexist with an additional 500 billion forint for healthcare. The goal remains a 3%-of-GDP deficit by 2030 against an estimated 7.5% this year.

Corporate supply is expected to recover after the subdued week: dealers anticipate about $30 billion of U.S. high-grade sales, largely bank borrowing after earnings, while nearly 80% of European survey participants expect more than €30 billion. Actual pricing and completion will show whether attractive yields are drawing sufficient capital as AI borrowers maintain their financing ambitions. Firmus's replacement funding, DayOne's access to new channels and Virgin Media's deleveraging choices remain distinct tests of that capacity.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries retreat and the curve flattens as household inflation expectations rise
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries surrendered part of their auction-led recovery on October 9 as higher household inflation expectations and expensive energy kept further Fed tightening in view. The 2-year yield rose 2.92 basis points to 4.7869% and the 10-year rose 1.1 basis points to 5.2378%, while the 30-year slipped 0.45 basis point to 5.5956%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 1.82 basis points to 45.09. At 10 years, real yields rose 2.23 basis points while breakeven inflation fell 1.13, placing the daily increase in inflation-adjusted financing costs. Benchmark yields nevertheless remained lower over the week.

Michigan's preliminary sentiment index fell to 46.3, with current conditions at a record low; nearer-horizon inflation expectations rose to 4.7% and the 5-year measure to 3.5%. Brent closed at $104.72 despite earlier relief. Equities recovered, and U.S. high-yield and hard-currency EM spreads tightened, but new positioning figures showed asset managers cutting ultra-long Treasury futures exposure.

European sovereign bonds stabilized while declining excess reserves and reluctance to use ECB refinancing facilities kept funding pressure in focus. Corporate access to capital remained uneven: Firmus withdrew its Australian listing and sought $2 billion to $3 billion of private financing, DayOne continued preliminary bond discussions, and Virgin Media O2's debt fell as regulatory scrutiny threatened a transaction expected to help deleveraging. High yields continued to attract buyers, but cash generation and contractual protections differentiated borrowers.
overall_summary.summary: Shorter maturities gave back part of the auction-led recovery as expensive energy and weaker household confidence complicated the Fed outlook, while the long bond held firmer and access to corporate capital remained sharply differentiated.
